item.title: Hida Mountains: Northern Alps Views from the Gifu Side — Guide
item.description: The Hida Mountains form the Gifu side of the Northern Japan Alps, rising to over 3,000 metres in dramatic peaks including Okuhotaka, Japan’s third-highest mountain, and offer some of the country’s most spectacular high-mountain scenery. The most accessible way to experience it is the Shinhotaka Ropeway, a double-decker cable car that climbs to a viewing platform at over 2,150 metres, delivering sweeping panoramas of the surrounding peaks without any hiking, while the Okuhida onsen villages below offer hot springs with mountain views.

item.title: Kamikochi: The Northern Alps' Pristine Alpine Valley — Guide
item.description: Kamikochi is a protected high-altitude valley in the Northern Japan Alps, roughly 1,500 metres above sea level, renowned for its pristine scenery: the clear Azusa River winding beneath towering peaks, the iconic Kappa Bridge, marshes and ponds, and forests carpeted with alpine wildflowers in summer. Private cars are banned to protect the fragile environment, so access is by bus or taxi only, and the valley offers everything from easy flat riverside walks and flower-viewing trails to serious mountaineering routes into the surrounding Alps, all within a genuinely spectacular natural setting.
